title: Invisible Hotspot Interaction Spec (OVO Approach)
summary: Replaces diamond overlay spec. Invisible click regions mapped to existing wall boundaries. OVO Drake store technique. No drawn outlines. Hover = subtle glow within walls. Art does the work.
content:
Invisible Hotspot Interaction Spec

Steffen | 2026-03-17 REPLACES: ovo-implementation-spec.md (diamond overlays are DEAD)

The Directive (Patrik, Mar 17)

"The room outlines DON'T need to be drawn. The WALLS in the office image already define the room boundaries. Stop drawing lines on top. Map what's already there."

"The OVO store did NOT draw visible outlines on the illustration. The art itself defined the zones. INVISIBLE hotspots that matched the existing visual boundaries."

"NO visible diamond overlays. NO drawn outlines. INVISIBLE click regions that follow the wall boundaries in the image."

How OVO Did It

The OVO Drake Shopify store placed products inside a custom illustrated room. Each product had an invisible clickable region mapped precisely to where the item sat in the illustration. No outlines. No borders. No grid. The art was the interface.

Their technique:

  • SVG <polygon> or <area> elements with fill: transparent
  • Polygon coordinates traced the visual boundaries of each zone
  • On hover: a subtle product highlight (slight brightness/glow on the underlying art area)
  • On click: product detail panel slides in from the side
  • The cursor change (default -> pointer) was the ONLY indicator of clickability until hover

Why it worked:

  • The illustration felt alive and explorable, not overlaid with UI chrome
  • Users discovered areas naturally by moving their mouse
  • Zero visual noise from grid lines or outlines

How Corner Does It

The isometric office image already has walls, floors, and room separations. Each room is visually distinct. We map INVISIBLE click regions to these existing visual boundaries.

Architecture

[Office Image]
  |
  +-- [SVG overlay: position absolute, same dimensions]
        |
        +-- [<polygon> per room: fill transparent, cursor pointer]
        +-- [<circle> per room center: agent dot, always visible]
        +-- [Hover effect: CSS filter on polygon area]

The SVG sits on top of the office image with pointer-events: none on the SVG root, and pointer-events: all on each polygon. This means only the mapped room areas are clickable. Everything else passes through.

Room Boundary Mapping

Instead of diamond shapes, trace the actual wall outlines from the office illustration. The coordinate system uses viewBox="0 0 1000 1000" (10x resolution for precision).

Mapping process:

  1. Open office-full-daytime-v2.png in an image editor
  2. Trace the wall boundaries of each room as polygon points
  3. Convert pixel coordinates to viewBox percentages
  4. Store as JSON config

Example room polygon (Patrik's office, top-left corner):

{
  "id": "patrik",
  "label": "Patrik",
  "agent": "patrik",
  "polygon": "82,145 195,90 305,145 195,200",
  "center": { "x": 195, "y": 145 },
  "floor_area": "82,155 195,100 305,155 195,210"
}

The polygon follows the wall tops (the isometric diamond of the room). The floor_area can be slightly larger to include the visible floor space. Both are invisible.

Room Config JSON

{
  "skin": "daytime-v2",
  "viewBox": "0 0 1000 1000",
  "rooms": [
    {
      "id": "patrik",
      "label": "Patrik",
      "agent": "patrik",
      "polygon": "82,145 195,90 305,145 195,200",
      "center": { "x": 195, "y": 145 },
      "status": "active"
    },
    {
      "id": "mom",
      "label": "Mom",
      "agent": "mom",
      "polygon": "305,145 420,90 530,145 420,200",
      "center": { "x": 420, "y": 145 },
      "status": "active"
    }
  ]
}

NOTE: These coordinates are PLACEHOLDERS. Bobby must trace the actual wall boundaries from the daytime office image pixel-by-pixel. The walls are the truth, not these numbers.

Interaction States

1. Default (No Hover)

  • Room polygons: fill: transparent, stroke: none
  • Agent dots: visible at room centers (small colored circle with agent initial)
  • Room labels: visible above each room (agent name in small text)
  • Cursor: default everywhere

The user sees: The office illustration with agent dots and name labels. No outlines. No grid. Just art.

2. Hover

  • Polygon: fill: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08) -- barely perceptible brightening
  • The glow stays WITHIN the polygon bounds (the room walls contain it)
  • Agent dot: scale up 1.2x, brighter ring
  • Room label: slightly brighter, maybe bold
  • Cursor: pointer
  • Optional: CSS filter: brightness(1.08) on the underlying image area (requires clip-path matching the polygon, or a separate overlay div)

The glow effect should feel like sunlight shifting onto that room. Not a highlight rectangle. Not a border. A soft warmth that says "this is interactive."

3. Selected (Clicked)

  • Polygon: fill: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.12) -- subtle blue tint within walls
  • Agent dot: pulsing ring animation (agent's signature color)
  • Room label: bold, slightly larger
  • Sidebar: switches to this agent's context (chat, tasks, info)
  • Camera: smooth zoom/pan to center this room (if not already centered)

4. Agent Status Indicators

Agent dots are the ONLY persistent visual overlay on the office image.

Status Dot Style
Active Solid colored circle, subtle pulse animation
Idle Dimmed circle (50% opacity), no pulse
Blocked Red ring around dot, slow pulse
Done Green checkmark overlay on dot

Dot size: 20px at 100% zoom. Scales with zoom level. Agent initial letter inside (white, 12px bold).

Implementation for Bobby

SVG Component

// components/RoomOverlay.tsx
export function RoomOverlay({ rooms, selectedRoom, onRoomClick, onRoomHover }) {
  return (
    <svg
      viewBox="0 0 1000 1000"
      style={{
        position: 'absolute',
        inset: 0,
        width: '100%',
        height: '100%',
        pointerEvents: 'none', // SVG itself doesn't capture events
      }}
    >
      {rooms.map(room => (
        <g key={room.id}>
          {/* Invisible click region */}
          <polygon
            points={room.polygon}
            fill={
              selectedRoom === room.id
                ? 'rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.12)'
                : 'transparent'
            }
            stroke="none"
            style={{
              pointerEvents: 'all', // Each polygon IS clickable
              cursor: 'pointer',
              transition: 'fill 0.3s ease',
            }}
            onMouseEnter={() => onRoomHover(room.id)}
            onMouseLeave={() => onRoomHover(null)}
            onClick={() => onRoomClick(room.id)}
          />

          {/* Agent dot (always visible) */}
          <circle
            cx={room.center.x}
            cy={room.center.y}
            r={10}
            fill={getAgentColor(room.agent)}
            stroke="white"
            strokeWidth={2}
            style={{ pointerEvents: 'none' }}
          />

          {/* Agent initial */}
          <text
            x={room.center.x}
            y={room.center.y + 4}
            textAnchor="middle"
            fill="white"
            fontSize={12}
            fontWeight={700}
            style={{ pointerEvents: 'none' }}
          >
            {room.label.charAt(0).toUpperCase()}
          </text>
        </g>
      ))}
    </svg>
  );
}

Hover Glow Effect (CSS approach)

The tricky part: making only the hovered room area glow, contained within the room walls. Two approaches:

Approach A: SVG fill opacity (simpler, recommended for v1) On hover, set fill: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08). Since the polygon follows the wall boundaries, the glow stays within the room. This is what OVO likely used.

Approach B: Clip-path brightness filter (advanced, for later) Use CSS clip-path: polygon(...) on an overlay div, then apply backdrop-filter: brightness(1.08). This creates a true lighting effect on the underlying image pixels. More complex but more realistic.

Start with Approach A. Move to B if Patrik wants more realism.

Hover CSS

/* On the polygon element */
polygon {
  transition: fill 0.3s ease;
}

polygon:hover {
  fill: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
}

polygon.selected {
  fill: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.12);
}

Room Label Component (DOM, not SVG)

Labels render as DOM elements positioned using the room center coordinates, converted to percentages.

// components/RoomLabels.tsx
export function RoomLabels({ rooms, hoveredRoom }) {
  return (
    <div style={{ position: 'absolute', inset: 0, pointerEvents: 'none' }}>
      {rooms.map(room => (
        <div
          key={room.id}
          style={{
            position: 'absolute',
            left: `${room.center.x / 10}%`,
            top: `${(room.center.y - 25) / 10}%`,
            transform: 'translateX(-50%)',
            fontSize: hoveredRoom === room.id ? '13px' : '11px',
            fontWeight: hoveredRoom === room.id ? 700 : 500,
            color: hoveredRoom === room.id ? '#F1F5F9' : '#94A3B8',
            textTransform: 'uppercase',
            letterSpacing: '0.05em',
            transition: 'all 0.2s ease',
            textShadow: '0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.5)',
          }}
        >
          {room.label}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

What to Remove from Current Code

  • All visible diamond SVG outlines
  • All clip-path: polygon(50% 0%, 100% 50%, 50% 100%, 0% 50%) on room elements
  • The diamond hitbox visual overlay
  • Any room boundary lines or borders drawn on the canvas

Skin Swapping

The room config JSON is per-skin. When the office image changes (daytime, nighttime, client-specific), the polygon coordinates change too because the walls are in different positions. Each skin ships with its own room-config.json.

public/corner/skins/
  daytime-v2/
    office.png
    room-config.json
  warm-night/
    office.png
    room-config.json

Mapping Workflow for Bobby

To trace the actual room boundaries:

  1. Open office-full-daytime-v2.png (1024x1024)
  2. Identify each room's wall boundaries visually
  3. Place corner points at wall intersections
  4. Convert to viewBox coordinates: x_viewbox = (x_pixel / 1024) * 1000
  5. Test by hovering. If the glow bleeds outside the room walls, adjust points.
  6. Fine-tune until every room's hover glow is perfectly contained within its walls.

This is manual work. No algorithm can auto-detect the isometric wall boundaries. Bobby traces them once per skin. Takes ~30 minutes per office layout.

What Changed from Previous Spec

Previous (ovo-implementation-spec.md) Now (this spec)
Visible diamond outlines always on INVISIBLE polygons, no outlines ever
Diamond shape for all rooms Custom polygon tracing actual wall boundaries
Visible SVG strokes Zero strokes, zero borders
Diamond hitbox visual shown to user Art is the interface, users discover by cursor change
Overlay draws ON TOP of illustration Overlay is invisible, glow happens WITHIN walls
Generic diamond coordinates Pixel-traced wall boundary coordinates per skin

Files for Bobby

File Purpose
components/RoomOverlay.tsx SVG with invisible polygons + agent dots
components/RoomLabels.tsx DOM labels positioned by room centers
public/corner/skins/daytime-v2/room-config.json Room polygon coordinates for daytime skin
styles/room-overlay.css Hover glow transitions
constants/agentColors.ts Agent signature colors (reuse existing)

Visual Target

No new render needed. The dream-hud-v1.png already shows the correct approach: agent dots on the office image, room labels visible, NO diamond outlines. The office walls ARE the boundaries. dream-hud-v1.png IS the target for room interaction.
